name: Unreal Tournament (1999)

scale.why: player cylinder 78 UU tall (CollisionHeight 39 x 2, Unreal Wiki: General Scale And Dimensions), scaled to 1.8 m: 0.02308 m/UU

speed.note: Classic speed; Hardcore (x1.1 game speed) 440, Turbo 560

dash_speed.note: UT's dodge (double-tap): a fixed 600 UU/s hop, 23 UU high; mapped to Quark's dash burst

jump.note: Classic; Hardcore (DeathMatchPlus's default, bHardCoreMode=True, DeathMatchPlus.uc#L1625) scales JumpZ x1.1 (#L1062-1063) and runs the game at x1.1 speed (#L139)

ground_accel.note: Unreal adds a fixed AccelRate (2048 UU/s2) up to GroundSpeed; Quark adds ground_accel x wish speed per second, so the same push is 2048 / 400

air_accel.note: if the air push is AirControl x AccelRate (717 UU/s2) toward AirSpeed: Quark-equivalent 0.35 x 2048 / 400 / 10; Unreal's native physics code isn't public (x0.0815 is outside the editor's 0.1..5 range: applying it clamps.)

air_cap.note: the air push aims at AirSpeed (the same as the run speed)

jumpHeightFromCode.note: v^2/2g from JumpZ and ZoneGravity: agrees with the measured 55 UU

airControl.note: UT's AirControl is a share of ground acceleration in the air; Quark's air_control isn't the same thing

notes: Speeds and heights measured by the Unreal Wiki community; gravity, JumpZ, AccelRate, AirControl and step from the UnrealScript defaults (UT 469b scripts, exported in Slipyx/UT99), which match the measurements (325^2 / 1900 = 55.6 UU against the measured 55). Ground / air acceleration are Quark-equivalents of Unreal's fixed-rate acceleration (estimated). UT's ground friction (ZoneGroundFriction 8, ZoneInfo.uc#L189) is a different formula and isn't mapped.

sources.title: Unreal Wiki: General Scale And Dimensions
